PLANNING COMMISSION
MEETING
Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability in compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act. Please contact the City Clerk at (310) 378-0383, at least 48 hours prior to the meeting to request a disability-related modification or accommodation.
Any person who has made campaign contributions to any of the members of the Planning Commission within twelve months before this meeting, should examine the provisions of Government Code Section 84308 which is posted on the bulletin board outside the Council Chamber.
We are advised by the members of the Commission that none of them have received campaign contributions within the last twelve months.
The applicant or any property owner entitled to notice of the hearing may, within fifteen days after the date of the Planning Commission decision, appeal the Planning Commission decision to the City Council (Ord. No. 091-529). A fee is required for filing an appeal with the City Clerkâ€™s office (R05-14).
The Council may, within fifteen days after the date of the decision or on or before the first date following the first Council meeting after the date of the Planning Commission decision, whichever occurs last: 1) Confirm the action of the Planning Commission and grant or deny the application; 2) Set the matter for public hearing and dispose of it in the same manner as on an appeal; or 3) Amend, modify, delete or add any condition of approval which the Council finds is not substantial under the circumstances relative to or affecting the property subject to the application for a development entitlement. Any determination of the Council pursuant to this paragraph shall be conclusive and final.
The Planning Commission reserves the right to modify the order of items shown on the agenda and advises all interested parties to arrive promptly at the commencement of the meeting.
Any person having any question concerning any agenda item may call the City Clerk to make inquiry concerning the item. Upon request, the agenda and, if any, documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability in compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act. Please contact the City Clerk at 310-378-0383, at least 24 hours prior to the meeting to request a disability-related modification or accommodation.
The Planning Commission welcomes and encourages public participation at meetings. This meeting will be held via videoconference only in order to reduce the risk of spreading COVID-19 and pursuant to AB 361 and the County of Los Angeles Public Health officer's recommended measures to promote social distancing. All votes taken during this teleconference meeting will be by roll call vote, and the vote will be publicly reported.
HOW TO VIEW THE MEETING: No physical location from which members of the public may observe the meeting and offer public comment will be provided. The meeting will not be livestreamed; however, the meeting will be recorded and made available on the City's website. You may attend the meeting through a computer or telephone:
ZOOM ID: 812 3253 4534
BY COMPUTER: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/81232534534
BY TELEPHONE: Call (669) 900-9128 and enter Zoom ID 812 3253 4534
ONE-TAP JOIN FROM MOBILE: +16699009128,,81232534534#
HOW TO PARTICIPATE BEFORE THE MEETING: Please submit your correspondence in writing to PlanningCommissionMeeting@pvestates.org. Comments received by NOON on Thursday, March 10, 2022 will be included with the posted agenda. Additional comments received by NOON on Tuesday, March 15, 2022 will be forwarded to the Commissioners and posted online as late correspondence. All correspondence submitted electronically via email will be provided to the legislative body, but will not be read aloud at the meeting.
HOW TO PARTICIPATE DURING THE MEETING: Members of the public are encouraged to participate under COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC or on any item of interest on the Agenda by simply utilizing the "Raise Hand" feature during the item under consideration. When called upon to speak please state your name for the record. Members of the public are not required to submit notification in advance.
Agenda reports and other disclosable public documents relating to each Agenda Item are available on the City's website under Planning Commission Meeting Agendas at www.pvestates.org.

MINUTES OF THE MARCH 15, 2022
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION
  OF THE CITY OF
  PALOS VERDES ESTATES, CALIFORNIA

A Teleconference meeting of the Palos Verdes Estates Planning Commission was held
via Zoom videoconference only in order to reduce the risk of spreading COVID-19 and
pursuant to AB 361 and the County of Los Angeles Public Health Officer’s
recommended measures to promote social distancing. Members of the public were
provided with the following information to provide public input:

ZOOM ID: 812 3253 4534
BY COMPUTER: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/81232534534
BY TELEPHONE: Call (669) 900-9128 and enter Zoom ID 812 3253 4534
ONE-TAP JOIN FROM MOBILE: +16699009128, 81232534534#

CALL TO ORDER: 5:35 p.m.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE Chairman Lazzaro led the Pledge of Allegiance

ROLL CALL

Present: Commissioners Thomas, Nendick, Walker, Wade, Lazzaro

Also Present: Acting Community Development Director Brady, Contract Planners Graham and
Wengert, Assistant City Attorney Crosthwaite, City Manager Prestwich

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

ACTION: Moved by Commissioner Wade, and seconded by Commissioner Nendick to approve
the agenda as presented. The motion unanimously carried by the following roll call vote:
AYES: Thomas, Nendick, Walker, Wade, Lazzaro
NOES: None

CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

City Manager Prestwich introduced himself to the Commission stating he looked forward to
meeting each of the Commissioners individually and thanked them for their service. Planning
Contractor Wengert introduced Sheryl Brady, the new Planner who is the Acting Community
Development Director.

COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

The following individuals addressed the Commission:
Frances McKindsey

CONSENT AGENDA

1.  Action Minutes from the meeting of February 15, 2022.

Commissioner Nendick requested the Minutes be clarified to include “no structures, walls,
pavement, and other improvements in the setbacks.”
 ACTION: Moved by Chair Lazzaro, and seconded by Commissioner Nendick, to approve the
Minutes of February 15, 2022, with the clarification requested by Commissioner Nendick. The
motion unanimously carried by the following roll call vote:
AYES: Thomas, Nendick, Walker, Wade, Lazzaro
NOES: None

PUBLIC HEARINGS (CONTINUED)

2.  M-1468-21; Miscellaneous Application for structures exceeding 8’ in height at the
  existing single-family residence located at 412 Via Almar. Lot 11, Block 1514, Tract
  6886. This project is exempt from CEQA pursuant to California Administrative Code
  Title 14, Chapter 3, section 15301.

  Applicant: Allan Rigg, 6415 Via Canada, Rancho Palos Verdes, CA 90275
  Owner: Kevin Farr
  Recommendation: Approve Resolution No. PCR-2021-1254 denying the application.

  Interim Director of Community Development Director Brady presented the staff report.

  The Public Hearing was opened.

  Applicant Kevin Farr addressed the Commission explaining his purpose for erecting the
  flagpole and requesting approval of the flagpole as presented.

  The following individuals addressed the Commission:
  Gregg Baetge
  Dominque Pheiffer
  Kristen Anderson

  The applicant was provided an opportunity to make additional comments. Mr. Farr
  indicated he had nothing further to add and thanked the Commission for their
  consideration.

  The Public Hearing was closed.

  The Commission deliberated on the issue and concluded the flagpole did not meet the
  necessary findings to allow the flagpole to remain.

  ACTION: Moved by Chair Lazzaro, and seconded by Vice Chair Wade, to adopt
  Resolution No. PCR-2021-1254 denying the application. The motion unanimously
  approved by the following roll call vote:
  AYES: Thomas, Nendick, Walker, Wade, Lazzaro
  NOES: None

3.  NC-1728-21 & G-1668-21; Neighborhood Compatibility and Grading applications for a
  new single-family residence located at 1201 Granvia Altamira. Lot 1, Block 4, Tract
  7538/8652. This project is exempt from CEQA pursuant to California Administrative
  Code Title 14, Chapter 3, section 15303.

  Applicant: Pritzkat and Johnson Architecture, 306 Vista Del Mar, Suite A Redondo
  Beach, CA 90277
  Owner: Sahil & Nidhi Sharma
  Recommendation: Adopt Resolution No. PCR-2022-1279 to approve the project as
  conditioned.

  A staff report was presented by Contract Planner Graham.

  The public hearing was opened.

  Applicant Keith Johnson of Prizkat and Johnson Architects addressed the Commission
  and presented slides showing the design of the project and the alterations that were made
  since the previous hearing and the proposed changes to be made to the project.

Planning Commission Minutes  March 15, 2022  2
   The following individuals addressed the Commission in opposition:
  Gordon Tsui
  John & Heather Aikin

  Applicant Keith Johnson responded and provided a summary of the proposed
  modifications of the project stating he felt the application meets and exceeds the approval
  previously given in 2018.

  The Commission asked questions of the applicant

  The public hearing was closed.

  The Commission deliberated and felt the application could be approved with the addition
  of the conditions and with the removal of Condition No. 2 in the Resolution.

  ACTION: Commissioner Nendick moved, and seconded by Vice Chair Wade, to
  approve the application with the following conditions: (1) remove from the Resolution
  Condition No. 2 Miscellaneous; (2) add a condition to lower the entrance way by one
  foot; and (3) add a condition to lower the chimney by two feet; and (4) add a condition
  to prohibit, structures, walls, pavement, or other improvements within the easement. The
  motion unanimously carried by the following roll call vote:
  AYES: Thomas, Nendick, Walker, Wade, Lazzaro
  NOES: None

4.  NC-1722-21, SC-141-21, G-16617-21, & CUP-109-21; Neighborhood Compatibility,
  Sports Court, Grading, and Conditional Use Permit applications for a new single-family
  residence and Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) located at 3609 Navajo Place. Lot 19,
  Block 1277, Tract 7140. This project is exempt from CEQA pursuant to California
  Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, section 15303.

  Applicant: Luis de Morales, Envirotechno Architecture, 116 S. Catalina Ave #102,
  Redondo Beach, CA 90277
  Owner: Mr. & Mrs. Lanza
  Recommendation: Adopt of resolution PCR-2021-1264 approving the application as
  proposed.

  Interim Community Director Brady presented the staff report.

  The Public Hearing was opened.

  Allan Rigg addressed the Commission on behalf of the applicant Luis de Morales,
  Environtechno Architecture. Mr. Rigg described the project and the modifications that
  were made from the original concept.

  The Commissioners asked questions of the applicant regarding the change in setbacks.

  The following individuals addressed the Commission in support of the application:
  Dawn Kaplan
  Ryan O’Toole
  Steve Lanza

  The applicant was provided an opportunity for rebuttal.

  The public hearing was closed.

  The Commission deliberated at length on the issues and discussed the issue of the
  underground sports court being converted to livable space, ADUs and whether a deed
  restriction was enforceable.

  ACTION: Moved by Chairman Lazzaro, and seconded by Commissioner Thomas, to
  adopt Resolution PCR-2021-1264 approving the application with the removal of

Planning Commission Minutes  March 15, 2022  3
   Condition 19; and added Conditions that the sports court area built underground within
  the home structure shall only be used as a sports court; and for the City Attorney to work
  with the applicant on the best solution to ensure that it remains a sports court; that the
  Planning Commission’s preference is a deed restriction be added voluntarily as offered
  by the applicant to help ensure that it is clear should the home be sold or otherwise
  transfer of ownership. The motion carried by the following roll call vote:
  AYES: Thomas, Walker, Wade, Lazzaro
  NOES: Nendick

5.  NC-1721-21 & G-1663-21; Neighborhood Compatibility, Miscellaneous, & Grading
  applications for a new single-family residence located at 1124 Granvia Altamira. Lot
  13, Block 1750, Tract 8652. This project is exempt from CEQA pursuant to California
  Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, Section 15303.

  Applicant: CBB Architects, Inc., 521 W. Rosecrans, Gardena, CA 90248
  Owner: Mike Hassani
  Recommendation: Adopt Resolution No. PCR-2022-1280 to approve the project as
  conditioned.

  Chairman Lazzaro recused himself due to a conflict of interest, turned the meeting over
  to Vice Chair Wade, and left the meeting.

  Contract Planner Graham presented the staff report.

  The Public Hearing was opened.

  Allan Rigg addressed the Commission on behalf of the Applicant describing the proposed
  modifications to the residence as proposed in the application.

  The Commission asked clarifying questions of the applicant.

  The Public Hearing was opened
.
  The following individuals addressed the Commission:
  John & Naomi McKissick
  Cy & Laura Parsa
  Mrs. Gomez

  The applicant was given an opportunity for further comment.

  The public hearing was closed.

  The Commission deliberated regarding the ridge height and the view impacts and
  concluded that the ridge line could be lowered.

  Re-opened public hearing to ask the applicant if he would agree to a two-foot reduction
  in the ridge line.

  The applicant was not and proposed a reduction of one foot on the highest ridge and six
  inches on the rear ridge with grading. The applicant acquiesced and agreed to the two-
  foot reduction.

  The public hearing was closed.

  ACTION: Vice Chair Wade moved, and seconded by Commissioner Thomas, to adopt
  and approve the Neighborhood Compatibility application at 1124 Granvia Altamira by
  Resolution No. PCR-2022-1280 subject to the following conditions: that the main ridge
  height at the center of the residence which is currently 117.25 be lowered by (2) two feet
  to 115.25; that vegetation on the property not exceed the adjacent eaves; all future
  vegetation be no higher than the adjacent eaves; and the vegetation within the setback
  adjacent to the east property line 1148 Granvia Altamira be no higher than three feet as

Planning Commission Minutes  March 15, 2022  4
   measured from the property line grade. The motion carried by the following roll call
  vote:
  AYES: Thomas, Nendick Walker, Wade,
  NOES: None
  RECUSED: Lazzaro

  The Commission recessed at 8:25 pm and reconvened at 8:30 pm, at which time Chair
  Lazzaro returned to the meeting.

6.  An Ordinance of the City of Palos Verdes Estates, California amending Section 18.20.010
  (La Venta Inn) of Chapter 18.20 (Specific Exceptions) of Title 18 (Zoning Regulations) of
  the Palos Verdes Estates Municipal Code and finding the action exempt from the California
  Environmental Quality Act.
  Recommendation: Continued to a Special Meeting of the Planning Commission via Zoom
  on March 29th 2022, at 5:30 P.M.

  ACTION: Moved by Chair Lazzaro, and seconded by Vice Chair Wade, to continue the
  Public Hearing of Item No 6 as noted above to a Special Meeting of the Planning Commission
  on March 29, 2022 at 5:30 PM. The motion unanimously carried by the following roll call
  vote:
  AYES: Thomas, Nendick, Walker, Wade, Lazzaro
  NOES: None

PUBLIC HEARINGS

7.  WTA-1-21; Consideration of Wireless Telecommunications Facility for a new small cell
  wireless facility within City right-of-way at 1409 Via Fernandez. This project is exempt
  from CEQA pursuant to California Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, Section
  15303.

  Applicant:  Crown Castle Fiber LLC, ATTN: Dat Dang, 200 Spectrum Center Drive,
  St. 1700 Irvine, CA 92618
  Owner:  City of Palos Verdes Estates

  Recommendation: Adopt Resolution No. PCR-2021-1282 to approve the project as
  conditioned.

  The staff report was presented by Contract Planner Graham. The Commissioner asked
  questions regarding the facility. The City Attorney advised that there is a criteria that
  has to be met and there are many restrictions as to what the City can or cannot do when
  it comes to wireless facilities.

  The Public Hearing was opened.

  Dat Dang addressed the Commission on behalf of Crown Castle Fiber LLC requesting
  approval of a small wireless facility in the public right-of-way at 1409 Via Fernandez to
  provide much needed E911voice and data coverage to the George Allen Baseball field
  and La Cresta community.

  The commissioners asked questions of the applicant. Chair Lazarro showed photographs
  of some of the facilities within the community that he did not feel was aesthetically
  acceptable.

  The following individuals addressed the Commission in opposition:
  George Trahan
  Mark
  Allan Rigg
  Vincent
  Mr. Sudarshan
  MaryLee

  The public hearing was closed.

Planning Commission Minutes  March 15, 2022  5
   The Commission suggested this item be continued to have Crown Castle look at
  alternatives and to look into leasing a city-owned poll and placing a wireless facility on
  that.

  ACTION: Chair Lazzaro moved, and seconded byVice Chair Wade, to continue the
  Public Hearing to the meeting of April 19, 2022, with a request to the applicant to
  consider alternative sites and to work with City staff to discuss those options. The motion
  unanimously carried by the following roll call vote.
  AYES: Thomas, Nendick, Walker, Wade, Lazzaro
  NOES: None

8.  NC-1724-21; Neighborhood Compatibility for an increase in the roof ridge elevation
  located at 1728 Addison Road. Lot 19, Block 1277, Tract 7140. This project is exempt
  from CEQA pursuant to California Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, section
  15303.

  Applicant: Danielle Zunzunegui, 296 Redondo Ave., Long Beach, CA 90803
  Owner: Dirk & Brittany Hofman
  Recommendation: Adopt Resolution No. PCR-2022-1283 to approve the project as
  conditioned.

  The staff report was presented by Interim Community Development Director Brady.

  The Public Hearing was opened.

  Applicant Danielle Zunzuneque of Jeff Jeanette Architects addressed the Commission
  describing the proposed modifications to be made.

  The following individuals addressed the Commission:
  Joe Hagen
  Fong Redihoff
  Thomas Ray

  The owners of the home were provided an opportunity to address the Commission
  explaining the purpose for the expansion of their home. The applicant and architect both
  provided additional information on the roof ridge elevation for the expansion.

  The Planning Commission asked clarifying questions of the Applicant.

  The public hearing was closed.

  The Planning Commission deliberated and requested that changes be made to the ridge
  line, and requested the applicant submit plans for the project.

  The Public Hearing was re-opened

  The Architect explained what they would have to do to change the ridge line and asked
  if it would be acceptable if they dropped the ridge line by two feet.

  The public hearing was closed.

  ACTION: Chair Lazzaro moved, and seconded by Commissioner Nendick, to continue
  the Public Hearing to the next Planning Commission meeting on April 19, 2022. The
  motion unanimously carried by the following roll call vote:
  AYES: Thomas, Nendick, Walker, Wade, Lazzaro
  NOES: None

9.  NC-1730-21, M-1513-21 & G-1673-22; Neighborhood Compatibility, Miscellaneous,
  & Grading applications for a new single-family residence located at 3661 Navajo Place.
  Lot NE ½ of Lot 213, Block 6104, Tract 8652. This project is exempt from CEQA
  pursuant to California Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, section 15303.

Planning Commission Minutes  March 15, 2022  6
   Applicant: Joseph Spierer, 707 Torrance Blvd., #100, Redondo Beach, CA 90277
  Owner: Benjamin & Melanie Archer
  Recommendation: Adopt Resolution No. PCR-2022-1284 to approve the project as
  conditioned.

  The staff report was presented by Planning Contractor Graham.

  The public hearing was opened.

  The applicant provided a description of the modifications that were being proposed for
  the single-family residence at 3661 Navajo Place. He presented slides of the
  neighborhood and how the home would fit within the neighborhood.

  The following individuals addressed the Commission in opposition:
  Mark & Laura Schenasi
  Steve
  William Melzer

  The applicant was given the opportunity to address the Commission. The owner Melanie
  Archer advised the Commission they were hoping that their application could be
  continued to have the opportunity to address as much of the feedback as possible.

  The public hearing was closed.

  The Commission deliberated noting the applicants were willing to make revisions. The
  Commission could not make findings that the application was compatible from
  perspective of scale with the neighborhood. The Commission concurred there was a lot
  of work to be done on the application.

  ACTION: Moved by Chair Lazzaro, and seconded by Vice Chair Wade to continue the
  public hearing. The motion unanimously carried by the following roll call vote:
  AYES: Thomas, Nendick, Walker, Wade, Lazzaro
  NOES: None

ITEMS OF INFORMATION

10.  Administrative Approvals.

ADJOURNMENT

Chairman Lazzaro thanked Commissioner Walker for her service and wished her the best. The
meeting was adjourned to the Special Meeting of March 29, 2022 at 5:30 pm.

Respectfully submitted

___________________________________
Sheryl Brady, Secretary

Planning Commission Minutes  March 15, 2022  7
